reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is ensuring that pytest's root collection operates within a strictly defined sandbox, preventing any spillover into detached worktrees or agent directories. This is formalized as a set-intersection problem: the workspace visited during any test function must be entirely contained within the designated root collection scope. The second primitive, the odds-payment circuit breaker, acts as a safety valve in high-stakes financial systems; it must fail conservatively (closed) when faced with database outages, modeled here as extreme anomaly scores. Both primitives rely on distinct but complementary verification metrics: the former tracks filesystem path uniqueness, while the latter monitors Type I error rates. The epistemic trace reveals a layered defense mechanism: the isolation primitive prevents contamination, while the circuit breaker contains failures when they inevitably occur. A veto condition exists if either primitive leaks information across boundaries, undermining the overall security posture.
